Sales invoices we issue are recorded as sales_invoice documents. Pull the number, issue date, seller, buyer (looked up by NIP), net amount, currency, and VAT rate code straight from the invoice. VAT = net × rate% ÷ 100, rounded half up to the grosz; gross = net + VAT; due date = issue date + payment days shown on the invoice. Status begins as open and may move to paid. Book each one in pl-stat: debit 201 for the gross, credit 701 for the net, credit 222 for the VAT.

So whenever we put out a sales invoice, what we're doing is creating a document of type sales_invoice, and we're grabbing all the key bits from it — the number, the issue date, who the seller is, who the buyer is with their NIP, the net amount, the currency, and the VAT rate code. From there, we work out the VAT by taking the net, multiplying it by the rate's percentage, dividing by 100, and rounding that result half up to the nearest grosz, and then the gross is just the net plus that VAT figure. The due date? That's the issue date with the payment days from the invoice added on top. The status kicks off as open and can eventually flip to paid. And for the bookkeeping side of things, everything goes into pl-stat: 201 gets debited for the gross, 701 gets credited for the net, and 222 gets credited for the VAT.

Complaints get logged with a number, customer, and details. Each one automatically triggers a case — type: case, subject set to the complaint number, status beginning at open and moveable to resolved.

So here's how it works: when a customer complaint comes in, you record it as a complaint document, and that document needs to carry the number, the customer, and all the relevant details. On top of that, every single complaint document has to open up a follow-up case — now this case is its own thing, it's got a type called case, its subject field holds the complaint number, and the status kicks off as open, though it can be switched over to resolved down the line.

Every complaint doc you create — number, customer, details — spins up a follow-up case straight away, type named case, subject filled in with that complaint number, status starting on open and flipping to resolved when it's sorted.
A withdrawn complaint gets its case closed as resolved.
